creators.name: Paul Bach-y-Rita
creators.bio: Neuroscientist who pioneered sensory substitution, from the 1969 tactile vision chair to the tongue-based BrainPort.
creators.bio_zh: 感官替代的开创者，从 1969 年的触觉视觉椅到基于舌头的 BrainPort。
creators.why: Showed the brain can learn to see through the skin, the premise of every new-sense device.
creators.why_zh: 证明大脑可以学会通过皮肤“看”，这是所有新感官装置的前提。

creators.name: Masahiko Inami
creators.role: Professor, University of Tokyo RCAST; JIZAI Body Project
creators.role_zh: 东京大学先端科学技术研究中心教授；JIZAI Body 项目负责人
creators.bio: Researcher in augmented humans, known for optical camouflage and the JIZAI Body project on freely reconfigurable bodies.
creators.bio_zh: 人类增强研究者，以光学迷彩和探索可自由重构身体的 JIZAI Body 项目闻名。
creators.why: Treats the body as editable: arms that can be added, swapped and shared between people.
creators.why_zh: 把身体当作可以编辑的对象：手臂可以增加、交换，也可以在人与人之间共享。

creators.name: Harpreet Sareen
creators.role_zh: 设计师与研究者，赛博格植物学
creators.bio: Designer (formerly MIT Media Lab Fluid Interfaces, now Parsons) who merges plants with electronics and robots.
creators.bio_zh: 设计师（曾在 MIT Media Lab Fluid Interfaces 组，现任教于 Parsons），把植物与电子和机器人融合。
creators.why: Gives plants machine bodies and uses plant tissue itself as circuitry.
creators.why_zh: 为植物配上机器身体，并把植物组织本身用作电路。

creators.name: Interactive Architecture Lab
creators.role: Research lab at The Bartlett, UCL, led by Ruairi Glynn
creators.role_zh: 伦敦大学学院巴特莱特建筑学院的研究实验室，由 Ruairi Glynn 领导
creators.bio: Master's programme and lab at The Bartlett working on responsive, robotic and living architecture.
creators.bio_zh: 巴特莱特建筑学院的硕士项目与实验室，研究响应式、机器人化与有生命的建筑。
creators.why: Built a roaming garden steered by its plants.
creators.why_zh: 打造了由植物自己掌舵、四处漫游的花园。

creators.name: Elke Reinhuber
creators.bio: Media artist and academic (City University of Hong Kong) working on expanded cinema and immersive media.
creators.bio_zh: 媒体艺术家与学者（香港城市大学），研究扩延电影与沉浸式媒介。
creators.why: Co-author of Green Rhythms, a human-plant symbiotic installation.
creators.why_zh: 人与植物共生装置 Green Rhythms 的共同作者。

works.title: Cyborg Antenna (Eyeborg)
works.description: An antenna osseointegrated into Neil Harbisson's skull turns light frequencies into vibrations he hears through bone, letting him perceive colour, including infrared and ultraviolet.
works.description_zh: 一根与 Neil Harbisson 颅骨骨整合的天线把光的频率转换为振动，他通过骨传导“听见”颜色，包括红外与紫外。
works.idea_en: A permanent new sense changes identity: Harbisson describes himself as a cyborg and his antenna as an organ.
works.idea_zh: 一种永久的新感官改变了身份：Harbisson 称自己为赛博格，称天线为一个器官。
works.method: A camera sensor at the tip of the antenna maps hue to sound frequency, transmitted by bone conduction through the skull implant; an internet link lets others send him colours.
works.method_zh: 天线末端的摄像传感器把色相映射为声音频率，经颅骨植入物以骨传导传递；互联网连接让他人可以向他发送颜色。

works.title: Seismic Sense
works.description: Implanted vibration sensors that let Moon Ribas feel earthquakes happening anywhere on Earth, their strength felt as vibration intensity.
works.description_zh: 植入的振动传感器让 Moon Ribas 感受到地球任何地方发生的地震，地震强度体现为振动的强弱。
works.idea_en: A body tuned to the planet: she senses the Earth moving all the time, far beyond the reach of human perception.
works.idea_zh: 一具与行星同频的身体：她时时刻刻感受到地球的运动，远远超出人类感知的范围。
works.method: Online seismograph data is sent to vibrating implants, first in her arm and later in her feet.
works.method_zh: 在线地震仪数据被发送到振动植入物，最初植入手臂，后来植入双脚。

works.title: Waiting for Earthquakes
works.description: A dance performance in which Moon Ribas stands still until her seismic sense detects an earthquake, then translates its intensity into movement.
works.description_zh: 一场舞蹈表演：Moon Ribas 静立等待，直到她的地震感官探测到地震，再把地震的强度转化为动作。
works.idea_en: The planet is the choreographer: a performance timed and scored by the Earth's movements.
works.idea_zh: 行星就是编舞者：这场表演的时间与节奏由地球的运动决定。
works.method: Real-time earthquake data from her seismic sense implants cues improvised movement on stage.
works.method_zh: 来自地震感官植入物的实时地震数据触发舞台上的即兴动作。

works.title: Weather Fins
works.description: Fins worn on the sides of Manel De Aguas's head sense atmospheric pressure, humidity and temperature and let him hear the weather as sound.
works.description_zh: 佩戴在 Manel De Aguas 头部两侧的“鳍”感知气压、湿度与温度，让他以声音的形式听见天气。
works.idea_en: The weather becomes a felt, continuous sense, closer to how many animals track the air.
works.idea_zh: 天气成为一种持续的、身体可感的感官，更接近许多动物感知空气的方式。
works.method: Environmental sensors in the fins drive sound transmitted by bone conduction; he also uses the data to compose music.
works.method_zh: 鳍中的环境传感器驱动经骨传导传递的声音；他也用这些数据作曲。

works.title: North Sense
works.description: A small silicone device attached to the chest with piercings that vibrates whenever the wearer faces magnetic north.
works.description_zh: 一个用穿刺固定在胸前的小型硅胶装置，佩戴者每次朝向磁北时它就会振动。
works.idea_en: Sold as a sense rather than a gadget: the aim is a direction sense that becomes part of perception.
works.idea_zh: 它被当作一种感官而非小工具出售：目标是让方向感成为感知的一部分。
works.method: A magnetometer and vibration motor in a silicone housing, fixed by two titanium bar piercings.
works.method_zh: 硅胶外壳内置磁力计与振动马达，通过两枚钛合金穿刺棒固定在身上。

works.title: feelSpace Belt: Learning the Sixth Sense
works.description: Participants wore a vibrating belt that always indicated magnetic north for six weeks, and some reported that their perception of space changed.
works.description_zh: 参与者连续六周佩戴一条始终指示磁北的振动腰带，其中一些人表示对空间的感知发生了变化。
works.idea_en: A magnetic sense can be learned: with time the belt stops being a signal and becomes part of how space feels.
works.idea_zh: 磁感官是可以学会的：随着时间推移，腰带不再是信号，而成为空间感的一部分。
works.method: A belt of 13 vibrotactile motors with an electronic compass continuously vibrates the element pointing north; navigation tests and interviews assessed learning.
works.method_zh: 一条装有 13 个振动马达和电子罗盘的腰带，始终让朝北的马达振动；以导航测试与访谈评估学习效果。

paper.title: Beyond sensory substitution—learning the sixth sense

works.title: Long-term Sensory Augmentation with a Magnetic Belt
works.description: A seven-week study of people wearing the feelSpace belt, combining behaviour, subjective reports and brain imaging to track how a new sense is learned.
works.description_zh: 一项为期七周的研究，结合行为、主观报告与脑成像，追踪佩戴 feelSpace 腰带的人如何学会一种新感官。
works.idea_en: Learning a new sense is learning new sensorimotor contingencies, and it reshapes both experience and brain activity.
works.idea_zh: 学会一种新感官，就是学会新的感觉运动关联，它同时重塑体验与大脑活动。
works.method: Participants wore the vibrotactile compass belt daily for seven weeks; brain imaging, behavioural tasks and questionnaires were compared with controls.
works.method_zh: 参与者连续七周每天佩戴振动罗盘腰带；以脑成像、行为任务和问卷与对照组比较。

paper.title: Learning New Sensorimotor Contingencies: Effects of Long-Term Use of Sensory Augmentation on the Brain and Conscious Perception

works.title: Sensory Augmentation with an Auditory Compass
works.description: People who wore an auditory compass signal for a period integrated it with their vestibular sense of rotation, showing a new sense merging with an old one.
works.description_zh: 佩戴听觉罗盘信号一段时间后，人们把它与前庭的旋转感融合，表明新感官可以并入旧感官。
works.idea_en: An artificial sense does not stay separate; it gets absorbed into the body's own sense of orientation.
works.idea_zh: 人工感官不会一直独立存在，它会被吸收进身体自身的方位感。
works.method: Headphones played a sound signal encoding the direction of north during a training period; perceived self-rotation was tested before and after (likely with passive rotation in darkness).
works.method_zh: 训练期间耳机播放编码北方方向的声音信号；在训练前后测试自我旋转的感知（可能是在黑暗中被动旋转）。

paper.title: Sensory augmentation: integration of an auditory compass signal into human perception of space

works.title: North Paw
works.description: An open-source anklet with a ring of vibration motors that buzzes on the side facing north, sold as a DIY kit.
works.description_zh: 一个开源脚环，环形排布的振动马达在朝北的一侧振动，以自制套件形式出售。
works.idea_en: A magnetic sense anyone can solder: umwelt expansion as a hobby kit.
works.idea_zh: 人人都能焊出来的磁感官：把环境界扩展做成业余套件。
works.method: A compass module drives eight vibration motors around the ankle; inspired by the feelSpace belt.
works.method_zh: 罗盘模块驱动脚踝周围的八个振动马达；灵感来自 feelSpace 腰带。

works.title: VEST (Versatile Extra-Sensory Transducer)
works.description: A vibrating vest that turns sound into patterns on the torso so deaf people can learn to understand speech through the skin; Eagleman proposed feeding it any data stream as a new sense.
works.description_zh: 一件把声音转成躯干振动图案的背心，让聋人能通过皮肤学会理解语音；Eagleman 还提出可向它输入任何数据流，作为新的感官。
works.idea_en: The skin can carry a new channel of the world: data becomes a felt sense after training.
works.idea_zh: 皮肤可以承载一条新的世界通道：经过训练，数据会成为可感知的感官。
works.method: An array of vibrotactile motors on a vest encodes audio frequencies spatially and temporally; the paper estimates how much information the skin can carry.
works.method_zh: 背心上的振动马达阵列以空间与时间模式编码声音频率；论文估算了皮肤能承载多少信息。

paper.title: Using space and time to encode vibrotactile information: toward an estimate of the skin's achievable throughput

works.title: SpiderSense
works.description: A suit with sensor modules that press on the skin when objects approach, letting blindfolded wearers sense their surroundings and even throw at targets.
works.description_zh: 一件装有传感模块的衣服，物体靠近时会压迫皮肤，让蒙眼的佩戴者感知周围环境，甚至能投掷命中目标。
works.idea_en: A whole-body proximity sense, like a spider feeling vibration, extends the skin into space.
works.idea_zh: 一种全身的接近感，像蜘蛛感知振动一样，把皮肤延伸到空间之中。
works.method: Ultrasonic distance sensors distributed around the body drive servo-actuated pressure pads, closer objects pressing harder.
works.method_zh: 分布在身体周围的超声波测距传感器驱动伺服压力垫，物体越近压得越重。

works.title: Haptic Radar
works.description: A headband of rangefinders and vibration motors that lets the wearer feel approaching objects around the head, an 'extended skin' that works without sight.
works.description_zh: 一条装有测距传感器与振动马达的头带，让佩戴者感受到头部周围逼近的物体，是一种无需视觉的“延伸皮肤”。
works.idea_en: Skin that reaches out into space: like whiskers or antennae for humans.
works.idea_zh: 向空间伸展的皮肤：如同人类的胡须或触角。
works.method: Infrared rangefinders on modular units map distance to vibration intensity on the scalp.
works.method_zh: 模块化单元上的红外测距器把距离映射为头皮上的振动强度。

paper.title: Augmenting spatial awareness with Haptic Radar

works.title: Phantom Terrains
works.description: Frank Swain's hearing aids were modified to stream the surrounding WiFi landscape as sound, letting him hear networks, their strength and their names as he walks.
works.description_zh: Frank Swain 的助听器被改造为把周围的 WiFi 环境实时转为声音，让他在行走时听见网络、信号强度和网络名称。
works.idea_en: A medical device becomes an organ for the invisible electromagnetic city.
works.idea_zh: 医疗设备成为感知不可见电磁城市的器官。
works.method: An iPhone app with sound artist Daniel Jones sonifies WiFi router data (signal, channel, encryption, names) and streams it to Bluetooth hearing aids.
works.method_zh: 与声音艺术家 Daniel Jones 合作的 iPhone 应用把 WiFi 路由器数据（信号、频道、加密方式、名称）声音化，并串流到蓝牙助听器。

works.title: Project Cyborg 2.0
works.description: Kevin Warwick had an electrode array implanted in his arm's median nerve, controlling a robot hand over the internet and receiving ultrasonic distance signals as a new sense.
works.description_zh: Kevin Warwick 在手臂正中神经中植入电极阵列，通过互联网控制机械手，并以超声波测距信号作为一种新感官。
works.idea_en: The nervous system wired straight to machines: a body that can extend across the internet and feel distance ultrasonically.
works.idea_zh: 神经系统直接连到机器：身体可以跨越互联网延伸，并以超声波感知距离。
works.method: A 100-electrode Utah array in the median nerve recorded and stimulated nerve signals, linked to a robot hand, an ultrasonic sensor and later to his wife's implant.
works.method_zh: 植入正中神经的 100 电极 Utah 阵列记录并刺激神经信号，连接机械手、超声波传感器，后来还连接到他妻子的植入物。

works.title: Eyeborg
works.description: Filmmaker Rob Spence replaced his lost eye with a prosthetic eye containing a wireless camera, recording and transmitting what it sees.
works.description_zh: 电影人 Rob Spence 用内置无线摄像头的义眼替换了失去的眼睛，记录并传输它看到的画面。
works.idea_en: The eye literally becomes a camera: seeing and recording collapse into one organ.
works.idea_zh: 眼睛真的变成了摄像机：看与记录合并为同一个器官。
works.method: A miniature low-resolution camera, battery and wireless transmitter fit inside an ocular prosthesis, streaming video to a receiver.
works.method_zh: 微型低分辨率摄像头、电池与无线发射器装在义眼中，把视频传到接收器。

works.title: Electrical Walks
works.description: Walkers wear special headphones that turn the electromagnetic fields of the city, from shop alarms to ATMs and lighting, into sound, following a map of hot spots.
works.description_zh: 行走者戴上特制耳机，沿着“热点”地图行走，耳机把城市里的电磁场——从商店防盗门到自动取款机与照明——转成声音。
works.idea_en: Walking with an electromagnetic ear reveals a hidden layer of the city that other senses miss.
works.idea_zh: 带着一只电磁之耳行走，会揭示其他感官错过的城市隐藏层。
works.method: Wireless headphones with induction coils pick up and amplify electromagnetic fields directly as audio.
works.method_zh: 带感应线圈的无线耳机直接拾取并放大电磁场，转为声音。

works.title: Architecture of Radio
works.description: A site-specific AR app that shows the cell towers, WiFi routers and satellites whose signals surround the viewer, as a 360° data landscape.
works.description_zh: 一款基于位置的 AR 应用，以 360° 数据景观呈现环绕观者的手机基站、WiFi 路由器和卫星信号。
works.idea_en: Seeing the radio spectrum around you turns infrastructure into a perceivable environment.
works.idea_zh: 看见身边的无线电频谱，就把基础设施变成了一个可感知的环境。
works.method: The phone's location and orientation sensors place data from open databases of cell towers, WiFi networks and satellites around the user.
works.method_zh: 手机的位置与方向传感器，把来自开放数据库的基站、WiFi 网络与卫星数据放置在用户周围。

works.title: Immaterials: Light Painting WiFi
works.description: A four-metre rod of lights that measures WiFi signal strength was walked through Oslo and photographed in long exposures, revealing the shape of invisible networks.
works.description_zh: 一根会测量 WiFi 信号强度的四米灯杆被带着走过奥斯陆，并以长曝光拍摄，揭示看不见的网络的形状。
works.idea_en: Making a machine sense visible in the city lets people see radio the way devices do.
works.idea_zh: 让一种机器感官在城市中变得可见，使人们能像设备那样“看见”无线电。
works.method: A rod of 80 LEDs displays measured WiFi signal strength as bar height while moved through streets during long-exposure photography; with Jørn Knutsen and Einar Sneve Martinussen.
works.method_zh: 由 80 颗 LED 组成的灯杆把测得的 WiFi 信号强度显示为光柱高度，在长曝光拍摄中被移动穿过街道；与 Jørn Knutsen、Einar Sneve Martinussen 合作。

works.title: PossessedHand
works.description: A forearm band that moves the wearer's fingers with electrical muscle stimulation, so a computer can play the hand like an instrument.
works.description_zh: 一条前臂绑带，以肌肉电刺激驱动佩戴者的手指，让计算机像演奏乐器一样控制这只手。
works.idea_en: Being moved by a computer from inside your own muscles: the hand becomes a machine output.
works.idea_zh: 从自己的肌肉内部被计算机驱动：手变成了机器的输出端。
works.method: Twenty-eight electrode pads on the forearm stimulate muscles to flex 16 finger joints.
works.method_zh: 前臂上的 28 个电极片刺激肌肉，使 16 个手指关节屈曲。

paper.title: PossessedHand: techniques for controlling human hands using electrical muscles stimuli

works.title: electric stimulus to face
works.description: Electrodes on the faces of Daito Manabe and friends were driven by music, making their facial muscles twitch in time with the beat.
works.description_zh: 真锅大度和朋友们脸上的电极由音乐驱动，使他们的面部肌肉随节拍抽动。
works.idea_en: A face becomes a display for a machine signal, performing expressions no one intended.
works.idea_zh: 人脸成为机器信号的显示器，做出无人刻意为之的表情。
works.method: Audio signals are converted to low-current electrical muscle stimulation delivered through electrode pads on the face.
works.method_zh: 音频信号被转换为低电流的肌肉电刺激，通过面部电极片传递。

works.title: Corpus Nil
works.description: A performance in which an AI system listens to the sounds and electrical signals of Donnarumma's muscles and turns them into light and sound, as the body slowly contorts.
works.description_zh: 一场表演：人工智能系统聆听 Donnarumma 肌肉发出的声音与电信号，并把它们转化为光与声，身体则缓慢扭曲。
works.idea_en: Body and algorithm shape each other; the performer is a hybrid organism with a machine.
works.idea_zh: 身体与算法彼此塑造；表演者是与机器结合的混合有机体。
works.method: Wearable mechanomyography and electromyography sensors feed a machine learning system that controls sound synthesis and lights in real time.
works.method_zh: 可穿戴的肌音图与肌电传感器把数据输入机器学习系统，实时控制声音合成与灯光。

works.title: The Uncomfortable
works.description: A series of everyday objects redesigned to be deliberately inconvenient: a fork made of chain, a watering can that pours on your feet, a chair you cannot sit in.
works.description_zh: 一系列被故意设计得不好用的日常物品：用链条做成的叉子、会浇到自己脚上的洒水壶、无法坐下的椅子。
works.idea_en: Breaking the fit between object and body makes us feel the object's own form and demands.
works.idea_zh: 打破物品与身体之间的契合，让我们感受到物品自身的形态与要求。
works.method: Mostly 3D-rendered images of redesigned objects, with a few physical prototypes.
works.method_zh: 主要是重新设计物品的 3D 渲染图，也有少量实物原型。

works.title: Seeking Comfort in an Uncomfortable Chair
works.description: A sequence of fourteen photographs in Domus in which Munari twists into ever odder positions in a modern armchair, searching for a comfortable way to sit.
works.description_zh: 刊登于 Domus 的十四张系列照片：Munari 在一把现代扶手椅中扭出越来越古怪的姿势，寻找舒服的坐法。
works.idea_en: The body bends to the object: a playful study of how a chair shapes the person who uses it.
works.idea_zh: 身体向物品弯折：一项关于椅子如何塑造使用者的游戏式研究。
works.method: Staged photographic series published in Domus no. 202 (1944).
works.method_zh: 摆拍的摄影系列，刊登于 Domus 第 202 期（1944）。

works.title: Thing Ethnography
works.description: Design researchers attached cameras and sensors to household things such as kettles, cups and fridges to see everyday life from the things' point of view.
works.description_zh: 设计研究者在水壶、杯子、冰箱等家用物品上安装摄像头与传感器，从物的视角观察日常生活。
works.idea_en: Things become co-ethnographers: an object's viewpoint reveals practices people do not notice.
works.idea_zh: 物成为共同的民族志研究者：物的视角揭示人们没有察觉的日常实践。
works.method: Autographer cameras and sensors mounted on objects captured images and use data, analysed with participants.
works.method_zh: 安装在物品上的 Autographer 相机与传感器采集图像和使用数据，并与参与者一起分析。

paper.title: Thing Ethnography: Doing Design Research with Non-Humans

works.title: Morse Things
works.description: A set of ceramic bowls and cups that live in people's homes and talk to each other in Morse code over the home network, mostly ignoring their human owners.
works.description_zh: 一组放在人们家中的陶瓷碗和杯子，它们通过家庭网络用摩尔斯电码彼此交谈，大多时候并不理会主人。
works.idea_en: Things with lives of their own: designing objects whose world is not centred on us.
works.idea_zh: 拥有自己生活的物：设计出世界并不以人为中心的物品。
works.method: Ceramic vessels with embedded single-board computers exchange Morse messages over WiFi and post to a Twitter account; deployed in homes.
works.method_zh: 内嵌单板计算机的陶瓷器皿通过 WiFi 互发摩尔斯讯息并发布到 Twitter 账号；部署在家庭中。

paper.title: Morse Things: A Design Inquiry into the Gap Between Things and Us

works.title: Affordance++
works.description: Objects communicate how they want to be used by moving the user's muscles: a spray can makes you shake it, a door handle tells you it is hot.
works.description_zh: 物品通过驱动使用者的肌肉来传达它们想被怎样使用：喷漆罐让你摇晃它，门把手告诉你它很烫。
works.idea_en: Taking the object's side: its behaviour is expressed through your body.
works.idea_zh: 站在物的一边：物的行为通过你的身体表达出来。
works.method: Electrical muscle stimulation on the forearm, triggered by object recognition and tracking, actuates wrist and finger movements.
works.method_zh: 由物体识别与追踪触发的前臂肌肉电刺激，驱动手腕与手指动作。

paper.title: Affordance++: Allowing Objects to Communicate Dynamic Use

works.title: Projecting Sensations to External Objects
works.description: When a table was stroked in sync with the participant's hidden hand, people felt the touch on the table and reacted physiologically when it was 'hurt'.
works.description_zh: 当桌子与参与者被遮住的手同步被抚摸时，人们感到触觉出现在桌子上，并在桌子“受伤”时产生生理反应。
works.idea_en: The body can extend into a plain object: ownership of a table, not just a rubber hand.
works.idea_zh: 身体可以延伸到一件普通物品中：不仅是橡胶手，一张桌子也能被“拥有”。
works.method: A rubber-hand-style paradigm in which the tabletop and the hidden hand were stroked in synchrony, after which the table was threatened while skin conductance was recorded.
works.method_zh: 采用类似橡胶手错觉的范式，同步抚摸桌面与被遮住的手，随后对桌子施加威胁，同时记录皮肤电反应。

paper.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 2003
paper.title: Projecting sensations to external objects: evidence from skin conductance response

works.title: Body-ownership for Actively Operated Non-corporeal Objects
works.description: People came to feel a virtual balloon or rectangle as part of their body when it moved in sync with their own hand.
works.description_zh: 当虚拟气球或矩形与自己的手同步运动时，人们逐渐把它感受为自己身体的一部分。
works.idea_en: Control, not shape, makes a thing feel like yours: an object can be embodied if it answers to your movement.
works.idea_zh: 让物感觉属于你的是控制而非形状：只要物回应你的动作，它就能被具身。
works.method: A data glove drove virtual objects on screen (likely a projection-based virtual-hand setup), comparing synchronous and asynchronous movement with ownership questionnaires.
works.method_zh: 数据手套驱动屏幕上的虚拟物体（可能是基于投影的虚拟手设置），以问卷比较同步与异步运动下的所有感。

paper.title: Body-ownership for actively operated non-corporeal objects

works.title: Ways of Machine Seeing
works.description: An essay that updates John Berger's Ways of Seeing for an age in which images are increasingly made and read by machines.
works.description_zh: 一篇为图像日益由机器生成与读取的时代更新 John Berger《观看之道》的文章。
works.idea_en: Machine seeing is also a way of seeing, shaped by power; any 'becoming machine' inherits it.
works.idea_zh: 机器的观看同样是一种观看之道，被权力塑造；任何“成为机器”的尝试都继承了它。
works.method: Critical essay in the journal APRJA, drawing on computer vision and Berger's television series.
works.method_zh: 发表于 APRJA 期刊的批评性文章，结合计算机视觉与 Berger 的电视系列。

works.title: The Machine to Be Another
works.description: Two participants wearing headsets see through each other's eyes and move in sync, experiencing the illusion of swapping bodies.
works.description_zh: 两名戴头显的参与者透过彼此的眼睛观看，并同步动作，体验身体互换的错觉。
works.idea_en: The human-to-human body swap: a baseline method, and a counterpoint, for works that try to swap into non-human bodies.
works.idea_zh: 人与人之间的身体交换：它既是尝试进入非人身体的作品的基础方法，也是它们的对照。
works.method: Head-mounted displays show a live first-person camera view from the other participant, with a performer mirroring movements and synchronised touch.
works.method_zh: 头显播放另一位参与者的实时第一人称摄像画面，配合表演者镜像动作与同步触碰。

works.title: MetaArms
works.description: A pair of robotic arms worn on the back and controlled by the wearer's feet, so that the body gains two extra arms driven by remapped legs.
works.description_zh: 一对背在身后、由佩戴者双脚控制的机械臂，身体由此获得两只由“重新映射”的腿来驱动的额外手臂。
works.idea_en: Remapping feet to arms shows how quickly the body schema adopts machine limbs.
works.idea_zh: 把脚映射为手臂，显示身体图式能多快地接纳机器肢体。
works.method: Foot position and toe bending, tracked by sensors, drive two backpack-mounted anthropomorphic arms; haptic feedback from the robot hands is returned to the feet.
works.method_zh: 传感器追踪脚的位置与脚趾弯曲，驱动两只背包式仿人机械臂；机械手的触觉反馈回传到脚上。

paper.title: MetaArms: Body Remapping Using Feet-Controlled Artificial Arms

works.title: JIZAI ARMS
works.description: A wearable base with sockets for detachable robotic arms that can be added, swapped between wearers and operated by other people, forming 'social digital cyborgs'.
works.description_zh: 一个带插口的可穿戴底座，可装卸的机械臂能被增加、在佩戴者之间交换，也可以由他人操作，形成“社会化的数字赛博格”。
works.idea_en: Robot limbs as social objects: a body that others can extend, lend and share.
works.idea_zh: 作为社交物件的机器肢体：一具可以由他人延伸、借出与共享的身体。
works.method: A backpack base with six sockets holds detachable robotic arms, teleoperated through scaled-down master arms; designed collaboratively with artists and users.
works.method_zh: 一个带六个插口的背负底座承载可拆卸机械臂，通过缩小比例的主控臂远程操作；与艺术家和使用者共同设计。

paper.title: Social Digital Cyborgs: The Collaborative Design Process of JIZAI ARMS

works.title: Elowan
works.description: A potted plant on a robotic base that uses its own electrical signals to drive itself toward light.
works.description_zh: 一株放在机器人底座上的盆栽植物，用自身的电信号驱动自己驶向光源。
works.idea_en: The plant gets a machine body: its bioelectric response to light becomes locomotion.
works.idea_zh: 植物获得一具机器身体：它对光的生物电反应变成了移动能力。
works.method: Electrodes on the leaves read the plant's bioelectrical responses to light; an amplifier and microcontroller turn them into motor commands for a wheeled base.
works.method_zh: 叶片上的电极读取植物对光的生物电反应；放大器与微控制器把信号转换为轮式底座的电机指令。

works.title: Cyborg Botany
works.description: Plants are augmented with conductive material grown inside their tissue so that the living plant can act as a sensor, display and actuator.
works.description_zh: 在植物组织内部生长出导电材料，使活的植物能够充当传感器、显示器和执行器。
works.idea_en: Not a robot next to a plant but circuitry inside it: the plant's own body becomes the interface.
works.idea_zh: 不是植物旁边放一台机器人，而是把电路长在植物里：植物自己的身体就是界面。
works.method: Conductive polymers are introduced into the plant's vascular tissue to form in-vivo wires, combined with the plant's natural signals and movements.
works.method_zh: 把导电聚合物引入植物的维管组织，形成活体内的导线，并结合植物本身的信号与运动。

paper.title: Cyborg Botany: Augmented Plants as Sensors, Displays and Actuators

works.title: Hortum machina, B
works.description: A geodesic sphere planted as a garden that can roll through the city, steered by the electrical signals of the plants it carries.
works.description_zh: 一个种满植物的测地线球体花园，可以在城市中滚动，由它所承载植物的电信号来掌舵。
works.idea_en: A garden becomes a cyborg vehicle: plants choose where their machine body goes.
works.idea_zh: 花园变成赛博格载具：植物决定它们的机器身体去往何处。
works.method: Electrophysiological sensors on the plants feed a controller that shifts the sphere's weight to roll it; part of the reEarth project at The Bartlett BPro.
works.method_zh: 植物上的电生理传感器把信号送入控制器，控制器移动球体重心使其滚动；属于巴特莱特 BPro 的 reEarth 项目。

works.title: Green Rhythms
works.description: An interactive installation that translates plants' circadian rhythm into light and air, with the carbon dioxide exhaled by visitors feeding a shared metabolic cycle.
works.description_zh: 一件互动装置，把植物的昼夜节律转化为光与空气，观众呼出的二氧化碳进入人与植物共享的代谢循环。
works.idea_en: Breathing with plants: visitors enter the plant's slow day-night timing through a shared exchange of light and air.
works.idea_zh: 与植物一起呼吸：观众通过光与空气的交换，进入植物缓慢的昼夜时间。
works.method: Environmental light and visitors' exhaled CO2 are sensed and used to stage photosynthesis and nocturnal gas exchange as light and airflow.
works.method_zh: 感测环境光与观众呼出的二氧化碳，以光与气流呈现光合作用和夜间气体交换。

paper.title: Green Rhythms: Symbiotic Interaction Between Humans and Plants

works.title: Tactile Vision Substitution System (TVSS)
works.description: Blind participants sat in a chair whose back pressed a grid of vibrating pins against their skin, driven by a camera they moved, and learned to recognise objects and faces through touch.
works.description_zh: 盲人参与者坐在一把椅子上，椅背上的振动针阵按压他们的背部，信号来自他们自己移动的摄像机；他们由此学会通过触觉识别物体和人脸。
works.idea_en: Seeing is done by the brain, not the eye: a camera and the skin of the back can form a new route to vision.
works.idea_zh: 看是大脑完成的，而不是眼睛：摄像机加上背部的皮肤，就能成为一条通往视觉的新路径。
works.method: A television camera's image was converted into a 20 × 20 array of vibrotactile stimulators on the back of a dental chair; active camera control was key to learning.
works.method_zh: 电视摄像机的画面被转换为牙科椅背上 20 × 20 的振动触觉刺激阵列；由使用者主动控制摄像机是学会的关键。

paper.title: Vision Substitution by Tactile Image Projection
